variants.subject: A round pavilion roof surveyed from directly above: its tile courses are concentric orbits round the ridge finial, one course per note of the span, and each drop that lands sits on its course like a planet, with the gutter as the outermost orbit where the puddle's held notes circle.
controls: rate: how many drop marks sit on the courses from the last bar (count): one or two at 0.25 a beat, about thirty at 8 a beat, newest brightest and older ones fading to hollow rings.
roof: how many concentric course rings the plan holds between finial and eave (count, plus ring spacing as position): one ring at 0 st, eight at 12, twenty-two at 36 crowding toward the 3 px floor.
gust: every drop mark slides round its orbit in the wind's direction (rotation about the finial, up to ±90° at full gust), with a bearing arc outside the gutter showing which way and how far.
puddle: beads collect on the gutter orbit, one per repeated note, joined by a link drawn along the gutter in the direction they replay (count): none at 0, a near-full ring at 100.
variants.reference: library/meikyu-orrery/README.md (concentric orbits round a body, built in 3D and projected; here the projection is straight down)
risks: A plan view throws away the depth that makes meikyu's orrery read as a solar system; at 1:1 it can read as a target, which craft.md names as an icon to avoid. The hips and survey labels are what stop it, and they're hairlines.
Rings are 10 px apart at 12 st but 3 px at 36 st; the roof control has to cap the drawn rings (one per scale octave degree, not per semitone) or it turns to hatching.
Gust and puddle are both empty at their defaults (0 and 0), so the rest frame shows neither; gust's rotation of the drops only reads once there are drops.
Orbits suggest a cycle, but rain isn't periodic; only puddle (the replay loop) is truly a cycle. The metaphor fits one control in four.
Muted state: the drops would have to go hollow and the finial dark; not yet drawn.

variants.subject: A mono-pitch roof cut in section like a patent figure, where each overlapping tile course is a pitch and a falling drop plays whichever course catches it, while the half-round gutter at the eave captures the run-off and its water level is how much of the last phrase gets replayed.
controls: rate: how many falling streaks hang over the roof at once (count): two at the slowest, about twenty at 8 a beat.
roof: the roof's pitch angle (rotation of the rafter, tiles and ridge post about the eave, 6° to 46°): a flat roof spans no notes, a steep one 36 semitones, so the ridge climbs about 60 px.
gust: the slant of every streak (shape/angle, ±35° from vertical) and where along the slope the drops land, bunching them toward the eave or the ridge.
puddle: the water line in the gutter section rises (position, 0 to 12 px) and drips hang from its lip, one per repeated note (count as second cue).
variants.reference: library/meikyu-capture/README.md (the machine's own rule drawn as a physical capture, with a wireframe ground and mid-grey labels)
risks: The capture is literal (a tile catches a drop) but weak as a rule picture: what the player most needs, which notes the roof spans, is only implied by course positions; there's no pitch axis without adding one.
Roof as pitch angle moves the whole roof (rafter, tiles, posts): a big redraw on a turn, though zero at rest.
The gutter is small and in the far corner from the brightest tile; the puddle control's whole effect lives in about 20 × 20 px, which will struggle against a score of 4.
Patent hatching at 6 px on a slanted rafter is close to the 3 px floor once rendered; check at 1:1 on the device.
Muted state: streaks stop above the roof (held mid-air in grey).

variants.subject: The roof itself is the loom: its tile columns are warp threads, one per note of the span, each bar of rain weaves a new row of tiles at the eave while older bars climb back toward the ridge, and a tile a drop struck stands up as a slab, solid where the puddle repeated it and wire where it was new.
controls: rate: how many raised slabs each row carries (count): one in a bar at the slowest, nearly every tile at 8 a beat.

roof: how many warp threads (tile columns) the roof is wide (count, the eave fascia and ridge lengthening with it as position): one column at 0 st, eight at 12, capped at sixteen with the header naming the real span.
gust: each older row's hits are shifted along the threads by the drift the wind gave them (position), so a gusty bar shears the slab pattern into a diagonal toward the ridge.

puddle: how many of a row's slabs are repeats of the row in front, drawn solid down the cloth (shade and count, solid vs wire): all wire behind the first row at 0, solid columns climbing to the ridge at 100.
variants.reference: library/loom-pages/README.md (steps as warp threads, passes as rows receding, solid = locked, wire = generated); library/toro-blocks/README.md for the hidden-line slab build
risks: Rows of slabs on a tile grid read close to a step grid, the panel craft.md warns about; the sloping roof plane and the eave/ridge are what make it a roof and not a sequencer matrix.
Rain has no bar structure of its own; rows-as-bars imposes one. Drops between bar lines need a rule for which row they land in.
Count is budget-heavy: 16 columns × 4 rows × 3 faces is 192 nodes before labels.
Roof and rate are both counts (threads vs slabs); they are different parts, but perceptibility has to show the thread count change isn't mistaken for density.
Muted state: the front row stays empty and every slab goes wire.

variants.subject: A star chart of the rain as a meteor shower: on a faint conic graticule the roof is a constellation, its tile courses plotted as stars up both slopes to the ridge, each drop a short trail traced back to a radiant the gust slides along the sky, with the puddle as an open cluster below the eave and the last sixteen beats ticked along the bottom strip.
controls: rate: how many meteor trails are plotted at once (count, 1 to ~24), each ending at the tile star it rang, with ticks filling the strip as second cue.
roof: the constellation's ridge star rises and more course stars appear up the slopes (shape, ridge moves ~50 px; count as second cue): a flat line of one star at 0 st, a steep gable at 36.
gust: the radiant slides along the top of the chart (position, ±150 px) and every trail swings to point back at it, so drops come in from the side the wind blows from.
puddle: stars gather inside the dotted cluster ring below the left eave, one per repeated note, and the cluster ring widens (count, then scale).
variants.reference: opxy/reference/field-and-figure.jpg (one bright figure on a low-grey field, activity strip along the bottom)
risks: The gable constellation is the house icon's outline in dots; it has to stay a constellation (broken lines short of each star, magnitudes, the name tegula) or it reads as clip-art.
Meteors fall away from a radiant, rain falls down: the picture asks the player to read drops as trails pointing up toward their source. Clever, maybe too clever.
Stars at 2–3 px on the upper courses sit at the small-part floor; the lint flags the cluster dots (1.8 px) and they'd need to grow.
The strip and the cluster are both secondary furniture in low greys at the bottom; together with the graticule labels the edges get busy.
Muted state: trails go out and the figure drops to the field's grey.

variants.subject: Stretch: a gable roof in hard one-bit ink, its tile courses printed as alternating dither bands under a 2 px bright outline, wired like an engineering schematic to labelled terminals for the rain streaks above it, the wind strokes beside it and the puddle plane at the downpipe foot.
controls: rate: how many flat rain-streak glyphs hang above the roof (count, 2 to ~20); the dither can't move, so the streaks are flat greys.
roof: the gable's pitch (shape: the ridge point rises from 20 to 90 px above the eaves), with the dithered course bands redrawn as static art per span step.
gust: the wind glyph's strokes lengthen to one side and every streak leans with them (shape, ±30°).
puddle: the flat puddle plane at the downpipe widens and lightens (scale 1× to 2×, two grey steps).
variants.reference: opxy/reference/toro-ink-rest.jpg (one-bit ink: 2 px outlines, ordered dither, a glyph per control)
risks: Doesn't fit, plainly. P9 is a hero figure for an engine; a player's screen should show the rule that picks notes, and a house with rain on it shows the setting, not the rule. Nothing on it says which tile is which pitch or what the puddle replays.

The exception case would be that rain is the one player whose rule is a picture people already know by sight (water on a roof); that holds for the concept but not the controls: the gable at 1:1 is the house icon.
Dither only lives in still art, but roof (the most visible control) changes the dithered planes: each span step would need its own pre-drawn dither set, or the bands go flat and the language is lost.
One-bit ink and schematic pull against each other: the terminals and labels read as a legend panel next to a picture (craft.md, Picture not panel).
The lint flags ~970 2 × 2 dither cells as under the small-part floor; that's the pattern's nature (toro-ink) but a warning wall.
Muted state: the outline drops to mid grey, the only element allowed to be brightest.
